blindSummary:
The country's principal LGBTIQA+ rights organisation formally denounced (14 October 2016) what it called "brutal and illegal acts of discrimination" at a public hospital in this state/province's main city: a trans woman had been interned in men's beds although public policy and the legal duty to treat trans people by their chosen name and social sex required the opposite - the complaint was lodged with the national health authority's regional office. (An earlier version of this record cited the then-applicable gender-identity law as the standard breached; that law took effect in December 2019, after the denunciation.) An emergency-room or inpatient visit here therefore carries a documented risk of gender-mismatched hospital placement. Separately, in January 2025 the main city's municipality dismissed the staff of its own diversity and non-discrimination office during honourary-staff cuts (~100 workers), which LGBTIQA+ organisations called a "dismantling" that left one person in post.

This state/province held 5.89 % of the national total of reported discrimination cases in 2024, the third-largest share. The two traveler-facing findings are the hospital bed placement (medical exposure) and the diversity-office dismantling (loss of local complaint infrastructure); unlike the country's most-populated region, whose documented problem is the sheer volume of cases (over half of all national reports), here the case share is normalised but accompanied by concrete institutional incidents.

The episode is institutional (health administration), not criminal.
